nodes.label: music_pref
nodes.rationale: Research library v0.1. This tree is only the offline foundation, so later behavior changes have to follow the named research documents and the locked decision record.

nodes.label: Bradley-Terry linear scorer
nodes.rationale: Begin with cosine similarity and L2-regularized pairwise logistic regression. Interaction features are required because concatenating audio and brief embeddings lets the brief-only term cancel in a pairwise comparison. Promote a neural head only if held-out results justify it; with 50-100 labels stay lower-dimensional and treat results as exploratory.

nodes.label: Frozen LAION larger CLAP music
nodes.rationale: Default encoder is revision-pinned laion/larger_clap_music because several attractive encoders impose noncommercial weight terms. This is a practical Apache-2.0 choice, not a claim that CLAP is universally best. Fallback is laion/clap-htsat-unfused. Precomputing embeddings is the economy, because the frozen encoder dominates download size, memory, and uncached latency.

nodes.label: Music Preference Model v0.1
nodes.rationale: A Python research library that learns separate brief-adherence and listener-preference rankings over 10-second excerpts, using frozen representations and the smallest scorer the evidence supports. The aim is a falsifiable personal tool and ML-engineering project, not a new general evaluator or a path to outperforming Suno.

nodes.label: AIME
nodes.rationale: Asks separate music-quality and text-alignment questions on 10-second regions. Useful precedent for keeping labels distinct, and a benchmark rather than personalization data.

nodes.label: Auditable acquisition procedure
nodes.rationale: Create an immutable asset record before preprocessing, with separate allowed, denied, or unknown permissions for research training, commercial training, audio redistribution, embedding redistribution, and learned-weight release, each with evidence. Hash original bytes and canonical PCM and track every descendant. Do not publish listener names, emails, detailed listening history, or free-text explanations by default.

nodes.label: CMI-Pref
nodes.rationale: 4,027 human votes and about 133.80 hours; the closest public task match for multimodal adherence. CMI-Pref-Pseudo is teacher distillation, not independent human preference. CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 keeps both in an isolated research lane, outside default permissive training. Paper and card pseudo-counts describe different units and must be pinned before use.

nodes.label: Dual-criterion annotation
nodes.rationale: Each pair collects independent brief adherence and personal preference, each A, B, tie, or cannot judge, plus per-candidate acceptability. Both unacceptable is not a preference tie, and cannot judge is not an uncertain vote. Preserve disagreements across listeners. The initial self-labeling study supports a claim about Justin on this distribution, not a universal preference model.

nodes.label: Music Arena
nodes.rationale: Cited monthly cards sum to 8,117 battles. The card is CC-BY-4.0, but some model audio is omitted and underlying source permissions still have to be filtered. Eligible only as a reviewed subset, never automatically the whole corpus, and not automatically as separate adherence labels.

nodes.label: P0 P1 P2 collection stages
nodes.rationale: P0 checks usability and stability on 20 brief families. P1 allocates 96, 16, 16, and 32 families to train, validation, calibration, and test before pairing, so families do not leak. P2 is a fresh confirmation set. After a random seed, uncertainty sampling stays inside training data, at least 30% of new queries stay uniform, and the locked test set is never actively selected. Teacher and synthetic labels stay separate from human judgments.

nodes.label: Candidate scorer interfaces
nodes.rationale: AudioTextEncoder and CandidateScorer are proposed protocols. The scorer consumes features, not paths or generator sessions. compare checks target, scope, listener support, and cache compatibility before scoring. train and evaluate consume persisted splits rather than inventing random splits. Calibration is a separate artifact bound to a checkpoint and scope.

nodes.label: Dual-target scoring
nodes.rationale: The explicit target is adherence or personal_preference. Rank scores candidates independently under one shared brief, model, and target, and does not average the two. If personal training is missing, that target is unsupported rather than silently replaced by generic quality. When a probability is enabled it always means P(A beats B), whichever candidate wins.

nodes.label: Generator adapter contract
nodes.rationale: An adapter returns immutable candidate ids, local audio, bounds, the original brief, seed, model revision, and rights records. Internal generator scores are generator-specific estimated evidence, separate from ranker outputs. The orchestrator must not treat a higher score as creative approval or rewrite prompts. Best-of-N and generator optimization are later work, and the API does not require ACE-Step, YuE2, or HeartMuLa.

nodes.label: JSONL manifest schemas
nodes.rationale: Assets, rights, briefs, clips, and judgments are UTF-8 JSONL; splits and reports are JSON; caches are NPZ with allow_pickle false; neural weights are Safetensors. Rights permissions are separate allowed, denied, or unknown fields, and the validator does not infer permission from a license string alone. Label source is human, teacher, or synthetic_rule and must not be mixed silently.

nodes.label: Model bundle provenance
nodes.rationale: A bundle carries weights or coefficients, feature and preprocessing specs, normalization, optional calibration, the training manifest, metrics, a model card, licenses, and checksums. It does not embed third-party encoders or source audio unless redistribution is separately allowed. Newly written Apache code does not make the end-to-end model Apache. A personal profile defaults to private.

nodes.label: music_pref release scope
nodes.rationale: The release is a Python library, CLI, manifest format, cached-feature pipeline, and model card. Package name music_pref is a placeholder, not a brand. Primary user is Justin as creator and researcher. Non-goals include generation, full-song structure, lyric fidelity, voice identity, reinforcement learning of a generator, and universal taste prediction.

nodes.label: Ten-second excerpt contract
nodes.rationale: Each candidate is explicitly bounded to ten seconds within a small tolerance. Short audio is not silently padded and long audio is not silently trimmed. Briefs that require an entire chorus arc fail the v0.1 scope check. Lyric fidelity and complete arrangement cannot be claimed from this window.

nodes.label: Evidence-gated roadmap
nodes.rationale: Phases run from recorded decisions, through the offline foundation and a P0 probe, to one locked P1 experiment, at most two predeclared expansions, then a rights-audited release. At 6-10 focused hours a week the core project is more plausibly 4-8 weeks than a weekend. Publish the engineering result even if the best model remains cosine or linear. Do not enlarge the study to rescue a preferred architecture.

nodes.label: 4.5 GB extraction guardrail
nodes.rationale: Stop extraction at 4.5 GB process RSS or sustained swap on the actual Mac. This is a project guardrail, not a documented hardware limit. Head-only timing must not be advertised as end-to-end latency. Reserve about 10-20 GB of disk and do not download whole multi-dataset archives.

nodes.label: MacBook Neo A18 Pro
nodes.rationale: The published configuration used for planning is an A18 Pro MacBook Neo with 8 GB unified memory. It can host an inexpensive cached-feature experiment and is not a platform for training a music foundation model. An Apple Neural Engine does not mean ordinary PyTorch uses it. No timing or memory benchmark has been run on this machine.

nodes.label: Three compute budgets
nodes.rationale: These are ceilings, not authorized jobs. Tier 1 is zero incremental cloud spend for a local pilot. Tier 2 is up to $50 after a measured bottleneck. Tier 3 is up to $250 only after a useful signal and a specific question. Quoted Runpod pod rates are arithmetic illustrations, not a job forecast. The easy waste is leaving a machine running or re-extracting the same audio.

nodes.label: Dummy encoder and feature cache
nodes.rationale: The first session ships a deterministic dummy encoder that cannot support production claims, plus a cache key covering content, excerpt, preprocessing, and encoder identity. Real embed calls are specified to return 512-dimensional finite arrays. No real CLAP adapter is in this session; zero-norm vectors are errors, not silent values.

nodes.label: First-session acceptance checklist
nodes.rationale: A clean checkout must install and test with no model downloads. Same-seed splits are byte-stable, the unsplittable graph fails, and identical inputs yield identical prepared audio and dummy features. The README must distinguish generated test signals from music or preference evidence, because a leakage bug would invalidate later modeling.

nodes.label: Leakage-safe component splits
nodes.rationale: Splits are seeded at the connected-component level across parent recordings, song families, hashes, both assets in a comparison, brief families, and repeated judgments. Connected records stay together. An unsplittable graph fails closed. Do not split a component to hit a ratio or fall back to random pair splitting.

nodes.label: Python 3.11 uv stack
nodes.rationale: Python 3.11 is the compatibility baseline so the package does not depend on a global 3.14 install. Core uses Pydantic, NumPy, soundfile, and SciPy. Torch, Transformers, and model downloads stay outside the core import path. Hydra, MLflow, a database, FastAPI, and Docker are unnecessary at this experiment count.

nodes.label: music_pref module layout
nodes.rationale: One module per real responsibility: schemas, manifest integrity, rights, identity, leakage-safe splits, audio preparation and diagnostics, encoder protocol, feature cache, linear and MLP scorers, training, grouped evaluation, inference, and a thin CLI. Media and caches stay out of Git.

nodes.label: Rights policy profiles
nodes.rationale: commercial_ready is the permissive default. research_only must be explicit and label output provenance; it is not a way to bypass permission that is still unknown for research itself. Unknown blocks the corresponding use. The fixture-only normalization profile must be rejected for a claimed level-matched experiment.

nodes.label: Adherence-preference disagreement benchmark
nodes.rationale: Can a small rights-cleared dataset reliably separate a candidate that follows the brief from one the creator likes more, and do existing models collapse that distinction? A carefully documented dataset with repeated judgments may be the strongest contribution.

nodes.label: Few-shot creator adaptation
nodes.rationale: Can a compact residual learn repeatable user-specific deviations from a generic ranker while abstaining on new styles or generators? Compare it with unadapted, nearest-neighbor, and regularized linear baselines on future unseen families. The question does not assume a Transformer or a new loss.

nodes.label: Unresolved source conflicts
nodes.rationale: Still unresolved: TuneJury's advertised permissive head versus noncommercial root code; CMI pseudo-count units; SongEval paper size versus released rows; MusicPrefs lacking an explicit dataset license; how many Music Arena pairs have both audio files and fit the ten-second policy; unverified HeartCLAP weights; MusicFM's sparse card; and unmeasured local pins, MPS parity, memory, and latency.

nodes.label: Primary source register
nodes.rationale: Bibliography of primary sources S01 through S54. Research cutoff is October 9, 2026 Pacific, with sources accessed October 10, 2026 UTC. Technical conclusions do not rely on third-party comparison blogs, and repository pages must be revision-pinned before implementation.

nodes.label: Bayesian Personalized Ranking
nodes.rationale: BPR established pairwise learning from implicit user-item feedback. Its optimization ideas are useful, but unobserved music must not be turned into negative artistic feedback.

nodes.label: CMI-RewardBench
nodes.rationale: Joint framework for musicality and instruction alignment. On the published text-only slice, CLAP-music scores 67.20% and CMI-RM 67.60%, which does not show that the gap is significant. Evaluate the intended input regime rather than copying a leaderboard winner.

nodes.label: MusicPrefs and MAD
nodes.rationale: Human comparisons warn that a convenient automatic metric may not match judgments. MAD correlates better than a standard FAD setting, but those figures are not per-pair accuracy, and prompts were withheld, so the labels are not adherence judgments. A collection-level score applied to one candidate is a category error.

nodes.label: TuneJury
nodes.rationale: Closest prior art: a 2.8M-parameter MLP over frozen CLAP/MERT features, with authors reporting 70.86% agreement on 2,035 held-out non-tie comparisons. A generic frozen-encoder ranker is not novel, and that number is not a transferable performance target.

nodes.label: Cheap falsification sequence
nodes.rationale: Validate rights and label meaning, test whether judgments are stable, benchmark one encoder locally, train simple models, then evaluate on locked data. Do not escalate if audio cannot be secured, the target is not repeatable, or the linear scorer fails to beat cosine. The first deliverable is an honest result.

nodes.label: Conditional GO
nodes.rationale: The cached-feature ranking architecture is feasible but already public, so the contribution has to come from the question, data, evaluation, or deployment. Proceed only while rights, repeatable judgments, and a real gain over strong baselines remain achievable.

nodes.label: Five-point gain gate
nodes.rationale: Proposed gate, not a prediction: at least a five-percentage-point gain over the strongest eligible baseline, with a positive lower bound on a paired group-resampled 95% confidence interval, on new brief and song families, plus a blind listening study. A 50-pair pilot cannot support a broad superiority claim.

nodes.label: Offline first Cursor session
nodes.rationale: The first implementation session is limited to typed manifests, rights-policy validation, group-safe splitting, deterministic audio preparation, a dummy encoder, and an offline contract test. It ends before real model downloads or training.

nodes.label: Independent focused library
nodes.rationale: Recommended vehicle is a narrow permissive library and small scorer built from established methods, with adapters toward existing benchmarks. Forking TuneJury stays comparison-only until licensing is resolved. Prefer the classical method if neural models do not help. Listening behavior, generated-music evaluation, and choice under a creator brief share ranking math but not labels or deployment.

nodes.label: Similarity is an alignment proxy
nodes.rationale: Contrastive audio-language embeddings help retrieval and broad attributes. They do not by themselves establish sensitivity to restraint, emotional authenticity, lyric correctness, or personal taste. An audio-only encoder has no native instruction representation, so text requires a learned interaction or a compatible aligned space.

nodes.label: TuneJury license adoption gate
nodes.rationale: The root LICENSE covers training and evaluation code under CC-BY-NC, while the model card advertises an Apache CLAP-only checkpoint. The checkpoint license must not be assumed to cover repository code. That conflict is an explicit adoption gate.

nodes.label: First-party data route
nodes.rationale: The releasable experiment uses original or explicitly contributed recordings, original briefs, and first-party judgments, optionally plus candidates from an audited permissive local generator. Public datasets remain separate approval scopes. A downloadable file, a service assigning output rights, and permission to train commercially are three different questions.

nodes.label: Rights lane policy
nodes.rationale: Unknown permission is a blocked state, not a guessed yes. The default is a permissive-only allowlist; restricted artifacts stay in a separate profile and directory, with no automatic mixing or distillation. Uncertain rights must not be laundered through cached embeddings or pseudo-labels. Where an effect on trained weights is not explicit, withhold a commercial-release claim.

nodes.label: Suno output exclusion
nodes.rationale: Suno terms effective September 3, 2026 prohibit using outputs or voice models to compete with Suno, including a competing music product. Because the stated long-term aim includes a competing platform, Suno output is excluded from training and the releasable benchmark unless written permission covers that use. This is a conservative project policy, not a claim that every private act of ranking is forbidden.

nodes.label: Typed abstention
nodes.rationale: Unsupported domain, an untrained personal target, an out-of-scope brief, an unresolved tie, or a thin margin must abstain or report unsupported. Those cases must not be compressed into a zero score. Validated probability stays null until scoped calibration; a raw sigmoid is research-only. Any recommendation stays provisional until a person accepts it.

nodes.label: CPU-first extraction policy
nodes.rationale: Extract with CPU first, one encoder per process, batch 1, FP32, and short clips, then test MPS against CPU for finite outputs and ranking consistency. Small heads do not need a rented GPU. Quantization, MLX, and Core ML are later parity-checked options.

nodes.label: Least expensive valid path
nodes.rationale: Complete the offline session, label P0 on original material, measure one CLAP extraction, and fit a compact linear baseline. That isolates label signal and local representation cost before buying hardware, renting a GPU, or generating thousands of songs.

nodes.label: Locked protocol changes
nodes.rationale: Do not casually change excerpt duration, label semantics, encoder or preprocessing identity, grouping rules, evaluation data, probability meaning, rights policy, or the primary success metric. A justified change needs a new protocol version and invalidates incompatible caches. Do not use the test set as validation. Human creative acceptance stays outside the model.

nodes.label: Offline foundation scope
nodes.rationale: The first session builds only the offline data foundation of the ranking library. It does not implement a generator, agent, web app, or paid training workflow, and it must not treat a neural model as already necessary. Fixture success is not evidence of preference prediction.

nodes.label: Brief-term cancellation
nodes.rationale: In a purely linear pairwise scorer the brief-only term cancels, so a nominally conditional model can ignore the instruction. Interaction features and shuffled-brief tests are the mitigation. This is treated as a mathematical fact, which is why the first trainable model is not a plain concatenation.

nodes.label: Project falsification criteria
nodes.rationale: The thesis fails if the target is not repeatable, simple baselines match learning inside the predeclared margin, gains vanish under grouping or within-generator evaluation, gains appear only on easy degradations, acceptable rights cannot be obtained, or the needed encoder is too large or restricted. Falsification should narrow the tool, produce an upstream contribution, or document a negative study.

nodes.label: Frozen embedding information gap
nodes.rationale: No head can reconstruct information the frozen representation discarded, so subtle emotion may be unreachable. The response is controlled counterexamples, an encoder probe, and narrow claims before any fine-tune.

nodes.label: Generator fingerprint shortcut
nodes.rationale: Apparent success can be recognition of which generator produced a clip, which then fails on unfamiliar generators. Provenance is stored, but generator identity is not a predictive feature. Within-generator tests and version holdouts are the check.

nodes.label: Reward hacking
nodes.rationale: Best-of-N filtering and reward optimization can select for the evaluator's own biases or collapse diversity. A higher score from the same model used to choose candidates is expected, not decisive. The MVP does not gradient-optimize a generator; usefulness requires new blind human judgments.

nodes.label: Author-reported results unreproduced
nodes.rationale: Published numbers in this review are author-reported and were not independently reproduced. Public file listings establish availability, not successful execution. No weight download, private service access, or paid compute occurred. Thresholds, parameter counts, and budget envelopes are this project's design, not claims by the cited authors.

nodes.label: Licenses do not certify upstream rights
nodes.norm_label: licenses do not certify upstream rights
nodes.rationale: A license statement refers only to the named artifact or page. It does not certify underlying composition, recording, or performer rights.

nodes.label: Dummy Encoder
nodes.rationale: A stand-in encoder belongs in the offline foundation so pipeline tests do not require downloaded weights.

nodes.label: Foundation Choices
nodes.rationale: Locked choices live in docs/decisions/0001-foundation-choices.md. Behavior changes also require reading docs/research/00_READ_ME.md and research documents 03, 04, 05, 06, and 08.

nodes.label: Incompetech Acquisition Shortlist
nodes.rationale: Twelve Kevin MacLeod tracks in groups P-01 through P-04, plus eight B-reserve tracks, are an acquisition plan under proposed rights record INC-BY-AI-2026-10-09, pending per-asset review. Crop bounds stay unset until audition. The reserve is not new listening families until matched alternatives are assembled. Catalog snapshot SHA-256 is 54802ad340562624b9d1c9c97aa9f005e2b9bf79001f8a1a07ed857e68b2164a.

nodes.label: Conditional Audio Sources
nodes.rationale: Owned originals, artist contributions, MusicNet, Musopen, Music Arena, and ACE-Step outputs stay conditional until provenance or an explicit grant is recorded. Music Arena contributes zero verified triplets and its votes are not our labels. ACE-Step generation is unnecessary for the first pilot, and its package MIT declaration is not a component-by-component warranty. Musopen's public-domain icon does not clear recording rights.

nodes.label: Incompetech Catalog
nodes.rationale: Kevin MacLeod's catalog is the strongest verified source because the creator offers it for AI training, publishes CC BY 4.0, and provides individual downloads, which is stronger than a dataset license badge. The live snapshot has 1,443 filenames and 87.14 hours; the older ~1,800-file offer is not the current count. Public embedding or head release is not expressly granted, and a private embedding does not cure unauthorized acquisition.

nodes.label: Adherence Preference and Acceptability Labels
nodes.rationale: Adherence, personal preference for this use, and acceptability of each candidate are separate questions. Tie and cannot_judge stay distinct from each other and from a missing answer; both-unacceptable is not a tie, and preference may conflict with adherence. Titles, artist, source, and automated scores stay hidden.

nodes.label: P0 Listening Protocol
nodes.rationale: Preserve 20 independent creative-brief families times 3 candidates, which is 60 clips and 60 within-family comparisons, plus 10 delayed repeats. Ten-second excerpts and separate label meanings stay unchanged. This is an N-of-1 usability and repeatability study, not evidence of neural superiority or calibrated probabilities, and it adds no train/test success claim. Feature caching before judgments is not permission to tune on those judgments.

nodes.label: Preliminary Four-Group Acquisition Test
nodes.rationale: Four groups from the rights audit, 12 recordings, and all three unordered comparisons plus two delayed repeats make 14 trials and about 11 to 18 minutes. This does not replace the 20-family P0, and its judgments stay in a separate dataset. P-03 and P-04 are related variants meant to expose comparisons that may be too easy or nearly identical, not evidence of broad artistic preference.

nodes.label: laion/clap-htsat-unfused
nodes.rationale: Resource fallback at revision 8fa0f1c6d0433df6e97c127f64b2a1d6c0dcda8a. The weight file is 614,525,833 bytes, about 20.9 percent smaller, with the same 512-d interface but a different feature space, so vectors must not be mixed and the cache namespace changes. Native LAION .pt checkpoints and the laion_clap package are a different route and must not be substituted.

nodes.label: Encoder Environment Pins
nodes.rationale: Candidate pins, not yet installation-tested, are Python 3.11, torch 2.14.1, and transformers 5.19.0, isolated from the Session 1 core environment so an optional encoder conflict does not rewrite it. The narrow array route needs no torchaudio, datasets, laion_clap, CUDA, or Accelerate. The probe runs outside the repository and, after hash check, with the hub offline.

nodes.label: laion/larger_clap_music
nodes.rationale: Primary encoder, pinned at revision a0b4534a14f58e20944452dff00a22a06ce629d1, because main or a short hash is not a reproducibility record. The weight is pytorch_model.bin at 776,444,665 bytes with published LFS SHA-256 5c289311f4a030d768af7ffbfdecd01b008aa64824211899a4e59f4f9d154fd1. HTSAT/Swin depths 2/2/12/2 project to 512 dimensions. The Apache-2.0 card does not clear training-data rights or prove there is no overlap with Incompetech. Load with restricted weights_only and without remote code; no safetensors file was published.

nodes.label: P-01 Three-File Acquisition Dry Run
nodes.rationale: The next bounded action is Disquiet, Mesmerize, and Colorless Aura, using the rights audit's official links and one ten-second region each under the listening protocol. It stops after three accepted asset, rights, and clip records or explicit rejections, to test whether the source yields one usable family while Session 1 finishes. The following step is the encoder benchmark, not generation, training, or a new annotation app.

nodes.label: First-Party Test Signals
nodes.rationale: These WAV and FLAC files are generated tones or noise for software tests of music_pref. They are not music recordings and not human preference judgments, so tests do not depend on real repertoire.

nodes.label: Fixture Manifest Rights Declaration
nodes.rationale: Rights fields on the fixture manifests record the generated-signal declaration explicitly, so a green test cannot be read as clearance of music.

nodes.label: Fixture Tests Are Not Preference Evidence
nodes.norm_label: fixture tests are not preference evidence
nodes.rationale: Fixture tests only exercise the offline data foundation. A passing test is not evidence that the system predicts musical preference.

nodes.label: Offline Foundation
nodes.rationale: The tree holds manifests, rights, identity splits, fixture audio preparation, and a dummy encoder. Model weights, training, and a generator stay out so fixture work cannot be mistaken for a preference model.

nodes.label: Protocol Version Lock
nodes.rationale: Excerpt length, grouping, rights, and label meaning are locked. Changing any of them needs a new protocol version so later comparisons stay interpretable.

nodes.label: Acquisition Manifest Review Procedure
nodes.rationale: The shortlist is metadata-verified, not audition-approved: HEAD returned HTTP 200 and no audio body was fetched. Each asset needs its own rights, crop, and permission fields, with unknown left unknown, because catalog capacity is ample and matching plus provenance are the bottleneck. Expected yield is 12 valid excerpts from 12 downloads, and up to 80 tracks to reach 60 candidates across 20 groups.

nodes.label: Conditional GO for Small Acquisition Test
nodes.norm_label: conditional go for small acquisition test
nodes.rationale: A small acquisition test can proceed because a rightsholder-level training offer was verified. P0 is still not assembled or cleared asset by asset, and no audio was downloaded or auditioned.

nodes.label: Jamendo AIME Suno and FreePD Exclusions
nodes.norm_label: jamendo aime suno and freepd exclusions
nodes.rationale: Jamendo's April 17, 2025 terms prohibit unauthorized commercial text and data mining, including AI, and MTG-Jamendo adds dataset-level restrictions. AIME mixes generated tracks, Jamendo recordings, and NC-SA tags, so rewriting tags does not clean provenance. Suno terms block using outputs to compete with Suno, including Suno audio inside another collection. FreePD's original site is closed, so a mirror is not equivalent clearance.

nodes.label: Source-Level Permissions Matrix
nodes.rationale: Research ML, commercial ML, audio release, embedding release, and trained-head release are separate columns so an unknown use stays Review and is never serialized as allowed. ML rights require the training offer plus the reproduction and adaptation grant; they are not inferred from free access.

nodes.label: Brief-Matched Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Retrieved catalog trios are brief-matched retrieval candidates, not three outputs generated from the same prompt, so the pilot can validate labeling and selection without supporting generator-specific claims. CLAP scores must not pick winners or curate difficulty. A single-artist pilot cannot show artist generalization; within-source matching only reduces source-quality shortcuts.

nodes.label: Independent Family Identity Rule
nodes.rationale: A recording, composition, alternate render, cover, or paraphrased brief cannot be reused across supposedly independent groups. The identity graph is inspected after selection; linked groups merge until 20 components remain. A collection tag is not proof of shared composition, while shared melody or arrangement is a reason to link. Five sourcing pools are pools, not a claim of 20 independent groups.

nodes.label: One-Musician Collection Method
nodes.rationale: A local player and a response table are enough; a new app is not a prerequisite. When the sole listener also selects clips, exposure is logged and coded randomized aliases are only partial blinding. P0 is three blocks of 20 trials plus 10 repeats 24 to 72 hours later, about 53 to 88 active minutes, planned as 2 to 4 hours. Ranking and acceptability answers are not independent comparisons.

nodes.label: Repeatability Pause Trigger
nodes.rationale: Ten repeats, sampled before votes are examined, are a coarse diagnostic only. Three or more strict reversals, or more than 20 percent cannot-judge, pauses scaling so instructions, crops, and fatigue are reviewed. Disagreements are never deleted to pass, and revised instructions need a new protocol version. These thresholds are operational, not a reliability claim.

nodes.label: Ten-Second Excerpt Preparation
nodes.rationale: Listening and CLAP share one 48 kHz mono derivative of exactly 480,000 samples so the embedding is what was heard. Gain-only matching targets -20 LUFS and a -1 dBTP ceiling; dynamic loudness normalization, compression, limiting, fades, padding, and automatic crops are forbidden. The order was implicit in the original package and is specified here. The CLAP processor sets the 48 kHz and 10-second contract; the audition procedure is this protocol. Stereo preference is out of scope.

nodes.label: Bounded CLAP CPU Benchmark
nodes.rationale: GO for a bounded CPU probe and NO-GO for claiming confirmed Mac feasibility, because specifications were checked and no weights were downloaded, no encoder ran, and no Mac benchmark was performed. Start with one cleared clip and brief, then 20 distinct clips; repeating one file does not count. CPU is the reference. MPS on 8 GB unified memory is optional and unproven. Numerical gates are project tolerances, not measured results. A CPU repeatability failure blocks feature caching; an MPS-only failure does not block CPU use.

nodes.label: Encoder Extraction Fallbacks
nodes.rationale: Smaller CLAP on CPU is first because it adds no service spend. One-time free Colab is next if capacity and upload permission exist. Paid rental is an estimate only and is not authorized. A lightweight audio-only model is not justified because it lacks equivalent text alignment; remote extraction is preferred to redesign. No permanent GPU hosting or hardware purchase is recommended.

nodes.label: CLAP Processing and Return Contract
nodes.rationale: Both processors specify 48 kHz, 480,000 samples, 10 seconds, 64 mel bands, FFT 1024, and hop 480, but those defaults do not authorize padding or cropping research items. The adapter accepts only a finite float32 mono waveform already prepared under the listening protocol. Transformers 5.19.0 returns pooler_output, the projected L2-normalized vector; logits include learned scaling and are not preference probabilities. Briefs over 512 tokens are rejected, and 514 is not the limit.

nodes.label: 4.5 GB RSS Guardrail
nodes.rationale: The existing guardrail is operationalized as 4,500,000,000 bytes including load, because the 1.5 to 4 GB RSS envelope is still an unverified plan and weight-file size is not peak RAM. Stop on exceedance or red pressure; pause on yellow pressure for 10 seconds or swap growth of at least 128 MiB. A 30-minute bound makes timeout inconclusive. Twenty clips in 10 minutes is a usability target, not a scientific success criterion.

nodes.label: Conditional Advance Without Training
nodes.rationale: Advance only to the smallest real-data test. A concrete source and a reproducible encoder spec now exist, but the listening set and Mac execution are unverified, so training does not start. A rights policy is not weakened to make the new source pass.

nodes.label: Data Conditional GO
nodes.rationale: CONDITIONAL GO covers the three-file acquisition test and later P0 curation. Declaring the full P0 ready, or publishing data and derived artifacts before asset-level review, is NO-GO. Evidence is the training offer, CC BY, the inspected catalog, and 20 live endpoints. Missing evidence is actual audio and QC, complete rights records, and 20 independent usable families.

nodes.label: Encoder CPU Probe GO
nodes.rationale: A supervised local CPU feasibility probe is GO after Session 1 and a cleared input. Claiming confirmed Mac deployment today is NO-GO. Official artifacts, revisions, the processor contract, current getter behavior, and an arm64 Python 3.11 wheel are verified. Peak memory, numerical stability, throughput, and A18 Pro MPS support remain empirical.

nodes.label: Data Foundation Encoder and Listening Gates
nodes.norm_label: data foundation encoder and listening gates
nodes.rationale: Four gates are ordered so a learning claim cannot precede cleared crops, a real Session 1 pass, a one-clip then 20-clip CPU probe, and a four-group listening test. MPS failure alone still permits CPU use. Expected service spend is zero, with 10 to 20 GB of free disk retained. A catalog composer credit does not clear arrangements or samples.

nodes.label: Ten Feasibility Decision Answers
nodes.rationale: P0 assembly is plausible and not yet demonstrated. The bottleneck is three musically plausible alternatives per brief with provenance and independent groups, not raw song count. CLAP on this Mac is an engineering hypothesis: 776 MB weights do not prove 8 GB headroom. Real embeddings may start after one cleared excerpt and a Session 1 pass; labeling all of P0 is not a prerequisite for that fit test.

nodes.label: Unchanged Research Baseline
nodes.rationale: Research documents 00, 01, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, and 10 remain the baseline. Unchanged are the 10-second scope, separate adherence preference and acceptability, ties and cannot-judge, ancestry grouping, the 20 by 3 design, P1 calibration gates, and a frozen encoder with baseline-first learning. Loudness and channel order is a proposed clarification to version before adopting. Operational thresholds in the listening and encoder handoffs are not scientific success gates. If the commercial_ready profile also requires release permission, finish that review instead of changing its meaning.

nodes.label: Passing Test Checks Offline Foundation Only
nodes.norm_label: passing test checks offline foundation only
nodes.rationale: A passing test only checks the offline data foundation. The signals are not evidence that a model predicts musical preference.
